results.primary_cause: Dry-bulk freight conditions appear to have strengthened in parts of 2026, but the available packet also describes the strength as potentially driven by rerouting and tightening vessel supply, while the exact current breadth and commodity-volume transmission remain unresolved.

supporting_evidence.claim: A key dry-bulk shipping-rate measure was reported at its highest level since December 2023, with the report attributing the move to rising Capesize demand and tightening ship supply.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Dry-Bulk Shipping Rates Hit Two-Year High on Capesize Demand

counter_evidence.claim: The prefetched BIMCO-related reporting warns that apparent 2026 dry-bulk strength may be substantially artificial and may reverse as rerouting effects normalize, implying material uncertainty about underlying commodity-volume demand.
counter_evidence.source_title: Dry bulk shipping faces 2027 supply glut: BIMCO warns Hormuz rerouting boost will reverse
